bottlenecks.pattern: serial accumulate chain with ripple carry
bottlenecks.root_cause: Three 40-bit additions are sequenced serially (s1 = s0 + p1; s2 = s1 + p2; s3 = s2 + p3), each depending on the result of the previous. Each addition implements carry ripple propagation, requiring ~40 logic levels per add.
bottlenecks.evidence: 86 combinational cells in path, 52 AOI/OAI cells (carry chain indicators), 12 XOR cells (sum bits); 87 stages in endpoint region contributing 2.0487 ns

bottlenecks.pattern: wide comparison with ternary mux at path end
bottlenecks.root_cause: 40-bit greater-than and less-than comparisons (s3 > LIMIT; s3 < -LIMIT) complete only after the full accumulation chain. The ternary mux selecting sat_val must then wait for these comparison results, serializing the comparison logic into the critical path.
bottlenecks.evidence: 12 OR3_X1 cells and additional AOI21 cells for wide comparison and mux tree; comparison logic embedded in the 87-stage endpoint region (mac_chain.v:81)

bottlenecks.root_cause: The b1_q input register output fans out heavily (fanout 42) to the 16-bit multiplier and downstream accumulator stages. High fanout increases transition time and degrades stage delay on this critical signal.
bottlenecks.evidence: fanout 42 at b1[0]_AND2_X1_A2_ZN_DFF_X1_D/Q with 1 stage exceeding fanout 8; contributes 2-stage startup delay of 0.2293 ns from mac_chain.v:28

summary: The critical path is a serial multiply-accumulate with saturation: b1_q feeds a multiplier to produce p1, which enters a three-stage ripple adder chain (s0 + p1 → s1 + p2 → s2 + p3), followed by a wide 40-bit comparison and ternary mux to select the saturated output. The serial accumulation chain with ripple carry dominates the delay, followed by the end-of-path saturation logic that must wait for all accumulation to complete.
